title: Console Conductor — pattern library for nested metric orchestration
creator: Amaya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a compact, reusable pattern (the 'Conductor') that reliably composes small metric components (metric chip, micro-sparkline, status chip, variant badge, and action affordance) into nested dashboard rows used across Rollouts and Cost Explorer. This ticket covers the Figma kit, token mappings, responsive behavior, and a consistency checklist for engineering handoff.

Background: Multiple Console surfaces display miniature dashboards (canary rollouts, per-model cost summaries, quick-compare lanes). Currently each surface reimplements spacing, alignment, and state behavior which has led to visual drift and duplicated engineering effort. The Conductor pattern centralizes layout rules, interaction language, and token usage so PM, Design, and Eng can reuse the same building block for various densities.

Proposed solution: Create a Conductor component in Figma with the following capabilities: (1) stacked row mode (single metric, optional sparklines), (2) compact lane mode (two-up metric pairs), (3) selectable runtime state (healthy / degraded / fallback) that surfaces a miniature status pill, (4) inline controls for rollout actions (pause, rollback, view) that appear on hover or keyboard focus, and (5) tokenized spacing & typography tied to the Console token library (density tokens, micro-typography, motion-presets).

Design constraints and trade-offs: Prioritize visual stability at small sizes (28–44px height lanes). Avoid adding heavy microcopy inside the pattern; surface only numeric summaries and a concise label. Motion should be subtle and limited (fade + translateY 4px) to avoid distraction in dense lists. Accessibility: ensure each conductor row is keyboard focusable, has a 48px touch target for action affordances, and exposes ARIA labels describing metric, timeframe, and state.

Deliverables: (a) Figma Conductor Kit (.fig) with all variants and tokenized components, (b) design documentation: token mapping guide and responsive rules, (c) annotated examples for Rollouts and Cost Explorer, (d) small dev-ready spec with CSS token names and sample React prop contract suggestions.
comments: 2025-01-16 — Kickoff with PM (Jonah Reyes). Alignment: Conductor should replace ad-hoc mini-dashboard in Rollouts and be the default for 'per-instance' cost rows.
2025-01-20 — Early prototype uploaded to Figma. Created three density variants (compact / default / spacious). Link: https://figma.com/file/Redwood/Conductor-Kit-2025#prototype

2025-01-28 — Review with Eng (Ethan Liu): requested explicit gap tokens (g-micro-1, g-micro-2) and explicit z-index rules for action popovers. Eng asked for static class names for focus outline so accessibility styles are consistent across apps.

2025-02-03 — Design review (Priya Nair): consolidated the status palette to use existing semantic tokens (state-success / state-warning / state-critical) and reduced motion duration from 160ms to 120ms for snappier feedback.

2025-02-10 — PM acceptance test: validated Conductor on a staging Rollouts view; discovered truncation issue at 320px width. Updated truncation rules: collapse label to initials + tooltip at narrow breakpoints.
2025-02-14 — Updated Figma library with documentation frames showing keyboard flows and accessible labeling patterns. Added explicit examples for RTL layout.
2025-02-18 — Engineering handoff prep: exported tokens JSON and added sample CSS variables in the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-design/pull/879
acceptance_criteria: Figma: Conductor Kit published to library with all density and runtime state variants
Token guide: mapping from Figma tokens to Console CSS variables (spacing, typography, color, motion) published in Confluence
Examples: At least two annotated examples (Rollouts use-case, Cost Explorer use-case) added to the design spec
Accessibility: Keyboard flows documented and validated by accessibility engineer (aria-label examples provided)
Engineering: A dev-ready spec including prop contract, CSS variable names, and a reference PR exists and is linked
notes: This pattern aims to reduce duplicated micro-dashboard implementations and speed up rollout of consistent metric lanes. Keep the API surface minimal — favor composition over configuration. Future follow-ups: add localized number formats and a variant for embedded charts (sparkline with threshold band).
